title: Equational vs Existential Copulas (हो vs छ)
subtitle: Distinguish between defining identity and stating location or temporary conditions.
keyPoint: Use हो (ho) to equate or define what something is, and छ (cha) to describe location, existence, or temporary physical qualities.

mistakes.note: Use छ (cha) for location, not हो (ho).
Nationalities and core identities require the equational verb हो/हुँ.
Variable physical states like temperature require छ (cha).

quiz.question: This is a pen. -> यो कलम ___।
quiz.explanation: Equating 'this' with 'a pen' is an identity statement, so 'हो' is required.

quiz.question: The tea is cold. -> चिया चिसो ___।
quiz.explanation: A physical condition like cold temperature requires 'छ'.

quiz.question: The keys are not on the table. -> चाबी टेबलमा ___।
quiz.explanation: Negating presence or location requires 'छैन'.

quiz.question: He is not a teacher. -> उहाँ शिक्षक ___।
quiz.explanation: For high honorific subjects (उहाँ), the negative equational copula is 'हुनुहुन्न'.

tip: Think of हो as an equals sign (=) and छ as expressing 'exists in a place or condition'.

title: Pronoun System and Honorific Tiers
subtitle: Navigate social politeness through low, medium, and high honorific levels.
keyPoint: Nepali pronouns strictly dictate matching verb endings to express social distance and respect.

mistakes.note: High honorific pronoun तपाईं must pair with the honorific verb ending -नुहुन्छ.
The ending -छस् belongs strictly to low tier तँ, not medium तिमी.
Respectful 3rd-person pronoun उहाँ requires high honorific verb agreement.

quiz.question: How are you? (Polite/Formal) -> ___ कस्तो हुनुहुन्छ?
quiz.explanation: The honorific ending 'हुनुहुन्छ' requires the high-respect pronoun 'तपाईं'.

quiz.question: What are you reading? (To a peer) -> तिमी के ___?
quiz.explanation: The medium pronoun 'तिमी' pairs with the suffix '-छौ'.

quiz.question: He/She is eating. (Formal third person) -> उहाँ खाना ___।
quiz.explanation: The respectful third-person pronoun 'उहाँ' takes the '-नुहुन्छ' verb form.

quiz.question: Where are you going? (Intimate/Low tier) -> ___ कहाँ जान्छस्?
quiz.explanation: The verb ending '-छस्' exclusively takes the low-tier pronoun 'तँ'.

tip: When in doubt with strangers or elders, always default to तपाईं (tapãĩ) and -नुहुन्छ to remain respectful.

title: The Ergative/Instrumental Marker (-ले)
subtitle: Mark the doer of completed transitive actions and the instrument used.
keyPoint: The postposition -ले marks the subject of transitive verbs in past/perfect tenses and indicates the instrument used for an action.

mistakes.note: Past transitive sentences require -ले on the subject.
The pronoun म combines with -ले irregularly to form मैले, never मले.
Intransitive verbs like जानु (to go) never take the ergative marker -ले.

quiz.question: I ate food. -> ___ भात खाएँ।
quiz.explanation: 'खाएँ' is past transitive, so 'म' changes to 'मैले'.

quiz.question: Ram wrote with a pen. -> रामले ___ लेख्यो।
quiz.explanation: The instrument used to perform an action takes the suffix '-ले'.

quiz.question: Hari went to the market. -> ___ बजार गयो।
quiz.explanation: 'जानु' (to go) is intransitive, so the subject 'हरि' must NOT take '-ले'.

quiz.question: What did you say? -> ___ के भन्यौ?
quiz.explanation: 'भन्नु' (to say) is transitive in the past tense, requiring 'तिमीले'.

tip: Check the verb: if it takes a direct object and happened in the past, attach -ले to the subject!

title: The Object Marker (-लाई)
subtitle: Distinguish recipients, human direct objects, and experiencer subjects.
keyPoint: Attach -लाई to indirect objects, specific human direct objects, and the subject in experiencer constructions.

mistakes.note: Inanimate non-specific direct objects like rice (भात) should not take -लाई.
Sensations like hunger and thirst require the experiencer marker -लाई on the subject.
Specific human direct objects normally require -लाई.

quiz.question: I am hungry. (Hunger struck me) -> ___ भोक लाग्यो।
quiz.explanation: Physical sensation predicates require the experiencer subject with '-लाई'.

quiz.question: Give this letter to the teacher. -> यो चिठी ___ दिनुहोस्।
quiz.explanation: The recipient/indirect object takes '-लाई'.

quiz.question: I eat apples every day. -> म सधैँ ___ खान्छु।
quiz.explanation: Inanimate, non-specific direct objects do not take '-लाई'.

quiz.question: Do you know Ram? -> के तिमी ___ चिन्छौ?
quiz.explanation: A specific person as a direct object requires '-लाई'.

tip: Never attach -लाई to inanimate things like food or inanimate tools unless you are personifying them.

title: Habitual Non-Past Tense (-छ/-छे/-छन्)
subtitle: Express daily routines, recurring habits, and universal truths.
keyPoint: Add habitual suffixes (-छु, -छौ, -छ, -छे, -छन्, -नुहुन्छ) directly to the verb stem matching the subject's gender and honorific tier.

mistakes.note: The first-person singular pronoun म requires the suffix -छु, not -छ.
Parents and elders should receive the high honorific suffix -नुहुन्छ.
A female third-person singular informal subject takes -छे.

quiz.question: I read a book every morning. -> म हरेक बिहान किताब ___।
quiz.explanation: The subject 'म' takes the first-person suffix '-छु'.

quiz.question: They live in Pokhara. -> उनीहरू पोखरामा ___।
quiz.explanation: Plural 3rd-person 'उनीहरू' agrees with '-छन्'.

quiz.question: You (high honorific) speak good English. -> तपाईं राम्रो अङ्ग्रेजी ___।
quiz.explanation: 'तपाईं' requires the honorific ending '-नुहुन्छ'.

quiz.question: My younger sister sings well. -> बहिनी राम्रो गीत ___।
quiz.explanation: Younger female family members take the feminine agreement ending '-छे'.

tip: For high honorifics (तपाईं/उहाँ), take the infinitive ending -नु and simply attach हुन्छ!

title: Basic Postpositions (-मा, -बाट, -देखि)
subtitle: Connecting locations, sources, and time points in Nepali
keyPoint: Nepali postpositions attach directly to the end of noun stems without spaces to indicate location, origin, or duration.

mistakes.note: Postpositions like -मा must be attached directly to the noun without a space.
Use -मा for static location ('on/at'), not -बाट ('from').
For physical origin of departure, -बाट is the natural native choice rather than -देखि.

quiz.question: The children are playing ___ the room.
quiz.explanation: The postposition -मा expresses location ('in the room').

quiz.question: He arrived ___ London yesterday.
quiz.explanation: The postposition -बाट indicates origin or point of departure ('from London').

quiz.question: I have been waiting here ___ morning.
quiz.explanation: The postposition -देखि marks temporal starting points ('since morning').

quiz.question: Water is falling ___ the roof.
quiz.explanation: Source of descent or movement away from a surface uses -बाट.

tip: Remember: -मा is stationary (where something is), while -बाट and -देखि denote movement or duration starting from a reference point.

title: Simple Past Tense (भयो / गरेँ)
subtitle: Narrating completed events and mastering ergative marking
keyPoint: In the simple past tense, transitive verbs require the subject to take the ergative particle -ले, while the verb agrees in gender, number, and honorific level.

mistakes.note: Because 'खाएँ' (ate) is transitive, the subject 'म' must take the ergative suffix -ले to become 'मैले'.
Intransitive verbs like 'आउनु' (to come) never take the ergative marker -ले.
Simple past negation of 'भयो' is simply 'भएन' without adding auxiliary forms.

quiz.question: I drank cold water.
quiz.explanation: Transitive past requires ergative 'मैले' and 1st person agreement 'पिएँ'.

quiz.question: Yesterday Sita went to the market.
quiz.explanation: 'गइन्' (went) is intransitive, so the subject must NOT take -ले.

quiz.question: Did you finish the work? (informal/mid-respect)
quiz.explanation: Transitive verb requires subject with -ले ('तिमीले') and mid-respect agreement 'गर्यौ'.

quiz.question: The program was not successful.
quiz.explanation: Negative simple past of 'भयो' is 'भएन'.

tip: Rule of thumb: Did the subject DO something to an object? Add -ले. Did the subject just move, sleep, or exist? No -ले.

title: Continuous Aspect with -दै (-दै छ)
subtitle: Expressing ongoing actions in the present and past
keyPoint: Attach the progressive converb -दै directly to the verb stem followed by a conjugated form of 'छ' or 'थियो' to indicate an ongoing action.

examples.en: पानी परिरहेको छ वा पर्दै छ।

mistakes.note: Do not double-inflect the finite verb; attach the continuous suffix -दै to the bare stem.
Vowel stems often take nasalization (ँ) when combined with -दै.
The auxiliary verb must agree with the plural subject 'उनीहरू'.

quiz.question: We are learning Nepali right now.
quiz.explanation: Subject 'हामी' matches the 1st person plural auxiliary 'छौँ'.

quiz.question: What were you (mid-honorific) doing yesterday?
quiz.explanation: Past progressive requires stem + -दै followed by past auxiliary 'थियौ'.

quiz.question: She (mid-polite) is singing a song.
quiz.explanation: Respectful feminine 3rd person takes 'गाउँदै छिन्'.

quiz.question: The boy is running in the field.
quiz.explanation: 3rd person masculine singular matches the auxiliary 'छ'.

tip: When -दै is doubled without an auxiliary (e.g., खाँदै खाँदै), it means doing something repeatedly or continuously while performing another verb.

title: Dative Experiencer Constructions (-लाई)
subtitle: Expressing needs, physical sensations, and involuntary feelings
keyPoint: Involuntary bodily sensations, desires, and necessities mark the human experiencer with -लाई, keeping the predicate in default 3rd-person neuter agreement.

useCases.label: Physical Pain (दुख्नु)
useCases.example: मेरो पेट दुखेको छ वा मलाई पेट दुख्यो।

mistakes.note: Needs require the dative experiencer marker -लाई on the person experiencing the need.
Feelings and bodily sensations require -लाई (मलाई, not म).
The verb agrees with the liked object (तिमी -> पर्छौ), not with the experiencer (मलाई).

quiz.question: Do you need help?
quiz.explanation: The experiencer of necessity takes -लाई ('तिमीलाई') and the verb remains 'चाहिन्छ'.

quiz.question: He feels sleepy.
quiz.explanation: Involuntary sensations like sleepiness take 'उसलाई ... लाग्यो'.

quiz.question: I like this book.
quiz.explanation: Experiencer takes 'मलाई', and the verb agrees with 3rd-person singular 'किताब' ('पर्छ').

quiz.question: We are feeling cold.
quiz.explanation: Cold sensations require the dative experiencer 'हामीलाई'.

tip: Think of -लाई as 'to me / for me'. You are not actively 'hunger-ing'; rather, 'hunger is happening TO you' (मलाई भोक लाग्यो).

title: Sequential Converb (-एर)
subtitle: Chaining chronologically ordered actions together
keyPoint: Add the suffix -एर to the verb stem to link sequential actions sharing the same subject, equivalent to 'having done X, Y happened'.

cells: Go to the market and buy vegetables.
Having woken up in the morning, I study.

examples.en: किताब पढेर उसले धेरै कुरा सिक्यो।

mistakes.note: While 'र' (and) exists, chaining identical-subject actions with -एर is vastly more idiomatic in Nepali.
-एर strictly requires both actions to share the same agent. Use -पछि for different subjects.
Irregular stem shift: 'धुनु' (to wash) becomes 'धोएर'.

quiz.question: Wash your hands and eat dinner.
quiz.explanation: Stem of धुनु alternates to धो- before adding the sequential converb -एर ('धोएर').

quiz.question: She woke up and drank water.
quiz.explanation: Same subject sequential action takes stem उठ्- + -एर = 'उठेर'.

quiz.question: Having reached Kathmandu, we rested.
options: हामी काठमाडौँ पुग्यो र आराम गर्यौँ।
quiz.explanation: Root पुग्- + -एर gives 'पुगेर' (having reached).

quiz.question: Go to school and study well.
quiz.explanation: The irregular stem for 'जानु' in the sequential converb is 'गएर'.

tip: Whenever you want to say 'did X and then did Y' with the same subject, reach for -एर instead of the conjunction 'र'.

title: Obligation and Compulsion (-नु पर्छ)
subtitle: Expressing 'must', 'have to', and 'should' using the infinitive
keyPoint: To express necessity or obligation in Nepali, attach the invariant verb पर्छ (present) or पर्यो (past) to the full infinitive ending in -नु, while marking the logical subject with the dative postposition -लाई.

cells: You do not have to come
He/She did not have to study

mistakes.note: Obligation constructions require the logical agent to take the dative marker -लाई (or an ergative instrumental context), not the plain nominative.
Always join पर्छ to the full dictionary infinitive ending in -नु, never to a conjugated finite verb form.
The negative of पर्छ is पर्दैन, not नपर्छ.

quiz.question: I have to read this book today.
quiz.explanation: The person with the obligation requires -लाई (मलाई) followed by the -नु infinitive plus पर्छ.

quiz.question: You do not have to go to the market tomorrow.
quiz.explanation: Present negative lack of necessity ('do not have to') uses -नु पर्दैन.

quiz.question: Yesterday we had to wait for a long time.
quiz.explanation: Past completed necessity ('had to') is expressed by pairing the -नु infinitive with the past form पर्यो.

quiz.question: What must Sita do right now?
quiz.explanation: Subject + लाई (सीतालाई) + question word + verb-नु पर्छ (गर्नुपर्छ) creates the question 'What must Sita do?'.

tip: Think of पर्छ as meaning 'it falls upon [someone]'; this explains why the person takes -लाई ('to me it falls to go').

title: Infinitive Forms (-नु vs -न)
subtitle: Distinguishing citation-noun forms (-नु) from purpose-motion forms (-न)
keyPoint: Use the -नु infinitive as a verbal noun, citation form, or subject of a sentence, but switch to the -न infinitive to express purpose before motion verbs or with auxiliary modal stems.

cells: Going or coming in order to do an action
Prepositions taking the oblique citation form

useCases.label: Subject / Gerund (-नु)
useCases.example: धुम्रपान गर्नु स्वास्थ्यको लागि हानिकारक छ।

useCases.label: Modal Ability with सक्नु (-न)
useCases.example: तिमी यो गह्रौँ भारी उठाउन सक्छौ?

examples.en: पौडी खेल्नु एउटा राम्रो कसरत हो।
ऊ नयाँ लुगा किन्न बजार गयो।
म आज बेलुका खाना पकाउन सक्दिनँ।
नेपाली भाषा सिक्नु निकै रमाइलो छ।

mistakes.note: When expressing the purpose of movement with motion verbs like जानु or आउनु, always change -नु to -न.
When the verb acts as the subject of the sentence (gerund), use the -नु form.
The modal auxiliary सक्नु ('can/able') must be preceded by the -न form, never the -नु form.

quiz.question: Learning Nepali is very interesting.
quiz.explanation: The subject of a sentence acting as a verbal noun ('learning') requires the citation infinitive -नु.

quiz.question: He went to the bazaar to buy vegetables.
quiz.explanation: Movement with a purpose ('in order to buy') triggers the purpose-infinitive ending in -न before verbs of motion.

quiz.question: Can you speak English?
quiz.explanation: The auxiliary verb सक्नु (to be able) requires the -न infinitive (बोल्न सक्नुहुन्छ).

quiz.question: They came to our house to eat food.
options: उनीहरू भात खानु हाम्रो घर आए।
उनीहरू भात खान हाम्रो घर आए।
उनीहरू भात खाएर हाम्रो घर आए।
उनीहरू भात खाने हाम्रो घर आए।
quiz.explanation: Expressing purpose of coming requires the -न form (खान आए).

tip: Whenever you can insert 'in order to' in English before a verb of motion or ability, use the -न infinitive in Nepali.

title: Unknown Past / Mirative Form (-एछ)
subtitle: Expressing newly discovered facts, realizations, and surprise
keyPoint: Attach -एछ (or its gender/honorific variants) directly to the verb root to signal that you did not witness an event occur but have just realized its result or discovered it with surprise.

cells: It rained! (I just noticed the wet ground)
Little sister has arrived! (I just saw her)
Apparently he didn't eat his meal.

examples.en: झ्याल खोलेर हेर्दा त हिउँ परेछ!
अहो! तिमी त निकै अग्लो भएछौ!

mistakes.note: Do not use -एछ for deliberate actions you consciously carried out in the past; use the simple past instead.

mistakes.wrong: पानी पर्यो! (when looking outside at puddles you just discovered)
mistakes.note: Use परेछ rather than पर्यो when you infer the past rain from fresh visual cues rather than experiencing the shower yourself.
The evidential suffix must agree with plural/honorific subjects (-एछन् for plural/mid-honorific).

quiz.question: Looking at the cold cup on the desk: 'Oh, the tea has gotten cold!'
quiz.explanation: The evidential -एछ conveys the immediate discovery of a state you were previously unaware of.

quiz.question: Opening your bag and realizing: 'I forgot my purse at home!'
quiz.explanation: First-person realization of an unintended slip of memory uses -एछु (मैले... बिर्सेछु).

quiz.question: Looking outside the window in the morning: 'Apparently it snowed last night!'
quiz.explanation: Deducing an unobserved weather event from morning evidence requires the evidential form परेछ.

quiz.question: Noticing your sister unexpectedly: 'Little sister has arrived!'
quiz.explanation: Feminine singular subjects take the feminine evidential agreement -इछिन् (or -इछे informal).

tip: Think of -एछ as the Nepali equivalent of saying 'Oh! It turns out that...' or 'I just realized that...'

title: Simultaneous Converb (-दा / -दाखेरी)
subtitle: Connecting concurrent background actions ('while doing') and situational conditions
keyPoint: Add -दा or -दाखेरी directly to the verb stem to link an ongoing background action with a main event, signifying 'while doing' or 'at the time of doing'.

useCases.label: Simultaneous Actions
useCases.example: गीत सुन्दै हिँड्दा समय बितेको पत्तै भएन।

useCases.label: Temporal Trigger / Concurrence
useCases.example: काठमाडौँ पुग्दा रातिको दश बजिसकेको थियो।

useCases.label: Conditional Instruction
useCases.example: गाह्रो पर्दा मलाई तुरुन्तै सम्पर्क गर्नुहोस्।

examples.en: बाटोमा हिँड्दाखेरी लडेर खुट्टामा चोट लाग्यो।
नेपालमा बस्दा मैले धेरै नयाँ साथीहरू बनाएँ।

mistakes.wrong: म खाना खाएर टिभी हेर्दा फोन आयो। (meaning at that very moment)
mistakes.note: Use -एर for sequential actions ('after doing'); use -दा for simultaneous interruptions ('while doing').
Verbs with irregular stems like जानु reduce to जाँदा (nasalized), not जान्दा.
Do not stack unnecessary auxiliary verbs; use -दा / -दाखेरी or duplicated -दै for concurrent parallel activities.

quiz.question: Be careful when crossing the road.
quiz.explanation: 'When/while crossing' expresses temporal circumstance and requires the stem + -दा form (काट्दा).

quiz.question: While going home, rain started falling.
quiz.explanation: The converb जाँदाखेरी ('while going') marks the ongoing action during which another event occurs.

quiz.question: Even though I searched a lot, I could not find my keys.
quiz.explanation: Stem + -दा पनि forms the concessive conditional 'even upon / even after searching'.

quiz.question: While studying, I fell asleep.
quiz.explanation: Simultaneous background activity ('while studying') uses पढ्दा.

tip: Contrasting with sequential -एर (do X then Y), the converb -दा means X and Y are occurring at the very same window of time.

title: Passive and Impersonal Voice (-इ- Stem Infix)
subtitle: Deriving passive verbs to diminish agency or convey general possibility
keyPoint: Insert the infix -इ- between the verb root and the inflectional ending to make any transitive verb passive, marking the original agent with -द्वारा or -बाट ('by').

examples.en: सडक मर्मतको काम द्रुत गतिमा गरिँदै छ।
यो औषधि दिनमा दुई पटक खाइन्छ।
नेपालमा विभिन्न चाडपर्वहरू हर्षोल्लासका साथ मनाइन्छ।

mistakes.note: If an agent is mentioned in a passive sentence, it must take -द्वारा or -बाट ('by'), not bare nominative.
The passive infix -इ- replaces the final mute vowel of the consonant stem, yielding पढिन्छ rather than पढ्इन्छ.
Nepali passive and impersonal verbs overwhelmingly default to the neutral third-person singular inflection (-इन्छ / -इयो).

quiz.question: What is this called in Nepali?
quiz.explanation: The passive idiom 'it is said / called' uses the stem भन्- + -इ- + -न्छ -> भनिन्छ.

quiz.question: The thief was caught by the police.
quiz.explanation: The passive agent takes -द्वारा ('by') and the verb takes the passive past marker समातियो.

quiz.question: From this viewpoint, Mt. Everest can be seen clearly.
quiz.explanation: Intransitive/impersonal capability 'is seen / is visible' uses the passive stem form देखिन्छ.

quiz.question: Festivals are celebrated with joy in Nepal.
quiz.explanation: Habitual general passive action ('are celebrated') takes the passive ending -इन्छ (मनाइन्छ).

tip: Passive forms in Nepali are frequently used where English uses 'one does...' or 'people say...' (e.g., भनिन्छ = 'it is said / they say').

title: Causative Verb Morphology (-आउनु / -वाउनु)
subtitle: Making or having someone else perform an action
keyPoint: Add -आउनु to basic consonant verb roots for direct causation, or -वाउनु for double or indirect causation involving an intermediary.

cells: to have something done via an intermediary
to feed / to cause to eat

useCases.label: Arranging Services via Third Parties
useCases.example: मैले सिकर्मीलाई टेबल बनाउन लगाएको छु।

examples.en: आमाले सानो बच्चालाई मीठो दूध खुवाउनुभयो।

mistakes.note: Basic transitive verbs cannot be used reflexively for 'feed'; use the causative verb खुवाउनु with the agent marker -ले.
To convey 'teach' or 'cause to read', use the causative पढाउनु rather than the basic transitive पढ्नु.
The recipient or causee being instructed must take the accusative/dative postposition -लाई.

quiz.question: Mother fed the child fresh milk: आमाले नानीलाई ताजा दूध ___।
quiz.explanation: The causative form of खानु (to eat) is खुवाउनु (to feed).

quiz.question: The teacher made the students write an essay: शिक्षकले विद्यार्थीहरूलाई निबन्ध ___।
quiz.explanation: लेखाउनु is the causative form of लेख्नु (to write), expressing causing someone to write.

quiz.question: I had my watch repaired by the technician: मैले मिस्त्रीद्वारा घडी ___।
quiz.explanation: Using गराउनु with the instrumental agent मिस्त्रीद्वारा marks an arranged, causative action.

quiz.question: Select the correct causative stem for the verb बस्नु (to sit):
quiz.explanation: The primary morphological causative derived directly from बस्नु is बसाउनु (or lexical बसाल्नु to settle/seat).

tip: Remember that the person causing the action always takes -ले in past/perfective frames, while the intermediate agent carrying out the action usually takes -लाई or -द्वारा.

title: Potentiality and Capability: सक्नु vs पाउनु
subtitle: Distinguishing sheer physical ability from granted permission and opportunity
keyPoint: Affix सक्नु directly to the bare verb root for physical ability, but use the infinitive in -न followed by पाउनु for opportunity, permission, or luck.

useCases.label: Physical or Mental Skill
useCases.example: म नेपाली भाषा सरर बोल्न सक्छु।

useCases.label: Fortunate Opportunity
useCases.example: दसैँमा घर जान पाउँदा म धेरै खुसी भएँ।

examples.en: उनी कठिन पहाडी बाटोमा पनि छिटो हिँड्न सक्छिन्।
मैले हिजो साथीहरूसँग रमाइलो चलचित्र हेर्न पाएँ।
के म यो शान्त कोठाभित्र अध्ययन गर्न सक्छु?
हामीले समयमै आफ्नो काम पूरा गरिसक्यौँ।

mistakes.wrong: मैले पोखरा जान सक्यो किनकि बिदा थियो।
mistakes.right: मैले पोखरा जान पाएँ किनकि बिदा थियो।
mistakes.note: Use पाउनु instead of सक्नु when referring to an opportunity granted by circumstances like having holidays.
Public prohibitions use the impersonal passive form of पाउनु (पाइँदैन), not सक्नु.

mistakes.wrong: म पौडिन पाएँ तर पानी चिसो थियो।
mistakes.right: म पौडिन सक्थेँ तर पानी चिसो थियो।
mistakes.note: Internal capability or theoretical ability requires सक्नु.

quiz.question: Because of heavy traffic, I couldn't reach on time: बाटो बन्द भएकाले म समयमा पुग्न ___।
quiz.explanation: Inability to achieve an action due to circumstance or capability uses सक्नु in the negative (सकिनँ).

quiz.question: Were you able to meet the minister yesterday (did you get the chance)?: के तपाईंले हिजो मन्त्रीलाई भेट्न ___?
quiz.explanation: Asking if someone had the privilege or opportunity to meet someone calls for पाउनु.

quiz.question: Photography is strictly forbidden here: यहाँ फोटो खिच्न ___।
quiz.explanation: Prohibitions and general permissions use impersonal forms of पाउनु: पाइँदैन indicates 'it is not permitted'.

quiz.question: She has already finished eating her meal: उनले खाना ___।
quiz.explanation: Auxiliary सक्नु compounded with the absolutive particple / root forms the completive aspect: खाइसकिन्.

tip: A neat mental check: if you can translate the sentence as 'I got to do it' or 'I had the privilege of doing it', reach for पाउनु; if it means 'I am physically/mentally capable', choose सक्नु.

title: High and Royal Honorifics (हजुर and -बक्सनु)
subtitle: Ultra-deferential speech registers for royalty, dignitaries, and refined formal contexts
keyPoint: Attach the auxiliary suffix -बक्सनु to oblique infinitive stems or honorific noun complements to express the highest possible social deference.

useCases.label: Polite Elite Speech in Traditional Homes

examples.en: उहाँ सवारी होइबक्सिन्छ कि भनेर पर्खिरहेका छौँ।
हजुरका कुरा सुनेर मलाई ज्यादै खुसी लाग्यो।

mistakes.note: Never use -बक्सनु or royal honorifics for oneself; they are strictly reserved for second and third persons of elevated status.
Combining the high-honorific pronoun हजुर with the lowest-grade verb suffix -छस् is a severe pragmatic clash.
In royal register, agents take बाट instead of the plain -ले, and speaking becomes हुकुम गरिबक्सनु.

quiz.question: May Your Highness please read this letter: हजुरले यो पत्र ___।
quiz.explanation: The optative/polite imperative form of the royal honorific is formed with stem + -इबक्सियोस् (पढिबक्सियोस्).

quiz.question: Which marker typically replaces the ergative agent -ले in high courtly royal statements?
quiz.explanation: The postposition -बाट ('from / by the graceful agency of') is characteristic of royal honorific agents.

quiz.question: The Queen arrived at the palace: महारानीबाट दरबारमा सवारी ___।
quiz.explanation: Royal arrival/movement uses the honorific compound सवारी हुनु / सवारी होइबक्सनु.

quiz.question: Why is 'मैले पत्र लेखिबक्सेँ' grammatically incorrect?
options: Royal honorifics cannot be applied to first-person subjects
quiz.explanation: Honorific affixes like -बक्सनु indicate deference toward the listener or topic and cannot elevate the speaker oneself.

tip: While -बक्सनु is less common in everyday modern democracy, it remains indispensable in classical Nepali literature, period films, diplomatic honors, and elite household traditions.

title: Compound Vector Verbs (हाल्नु, दिनु, लिनु, छोड्नु)
subtitle: Adding nuance, trajectory, and suddenness through auxiliary vector verbs
keyPoint: Combine an absolutive primary verb stem in -इ with a vector auxiliary to specify beneficiary, sudden finality, or irrevocable completion.

cells: Action performed for someone else's benefit
Action performed for one's own benefit
Persistence to the bitter end or uninhibited result
to do at all costs / finish irrevocably

useCases.label: Immediate / Decisive Action
useCases.example: पानी पर्न थाल्यो, छिटो छाता ओढीहाल।

useCases.label: Determined Completion
useCases.example: जतिसुकै गाह्रो भए पनि म यो काम फत्ते गरिछोड्छु।

examples.en: उनले आफ्नो सबै कुरा मनमै राखिलिइन्।
समय सकिन लाग्यो, छिटो भात खाइहालौँ।

mistakes.note: लिनु marks an action done for oneself; an action done for another person requires दिनु.

mistakes.wrong: उहाँले मलाई सहयोग गरिहाल्नुभयो (meaning 'kindly helped me').
mistakes.note: हाल्नु implies haste or recklessness; for polite benevolence use गरिदिनु.
The primary verb must take the conjunctive/absolutive -इ stem (गरि-) before the auxiliary छोड्नु.

quiz.question: Could you please explain this word for me?: कृपया मलाई यो शब्द ___।
quiz.explanation: दिनु as a vector verb conveys an action performed for the benefit of the speaker/listener (benefactive).

quiz.question: The child finished the entire plate of food rapidly and completely: बच्चाले सबै खाना ___।
quiz.explanation: हाल्नु signifies swift, unhesitating, or decisive action.

quiz.question: No matter how difficult the exam, he will pass it at all costs: ऊ परीक्षा उत्तीर्ण ___।
quiz.explanation: छोड्नु used as a vector auxiliary indicates unshakable resolve and persistence to completion.

quiz.question: I purchased and secured that land for myself: मैले त्यो जग्गा ___।
quiz.explanation: लिनु denotes reflexive benefit—performing the action primarily for oneself.

tip: Think of compound vectors as directional arrows: दिनु points outwards to bless someone else, while लिनु bends inwards to retain the benefit for the doer.

title: Hypothetical and Counterfactual Conditionals (-ए / -एदेखि ... -थियो)
subtitle: Navigating real, unreal, and past counterfactual conditional statements
keyPoint: Suffix -ए or -एदेखि to the condition verb root and use the past habitual/imperfect suffix -थियो in the result clause to express counterfactual conditions.

cells: If it rains, we will stay.
If you studied, you would learn.
If he had come, I would have met him.
If it hadn't rained, we would have gone.

useCases.label: Past Regrets and Unfulfilled Events
useCases.example: समयमै डाक्टरकहाँ गएको भए बिरामी बाँच्नेथियो।

useCases.label: Hypothetical Future Scenarios
useCases.example: पैसा भए त म संसार घुम्न जानेथिएँ।

useCases.label: Everyday Conversational Contingency
useCases.example: भोलि घाम लागे हामी वनभोज जान्छौँ।

examples.en: तिमीले मिहिनेत गरेको भए परीक्षामा उत्तीर्ण हुनेथियौ।
पानी नपरेको भए हामी समयमै पोखरा पुग्नेथियौँ।
उसले मलाई बोलाएदेखि म अवश्य जानेथिएँ।
राम्रोसँग सोचेको भए यस्तो गल्ती हुने थिएन।
सत्य बोलेको भए कसैले तिमीलाई गाली गर्ने थिएन।

mistakes.wrong: यदि म धनी भयो भने म गाडी किन्थ्यो।
mistakes.right: यदि म धनी भएको भए गाडी किन्नेथिएँ।
mistakes.note: Counterfactual 'would have' conditions require the past conditional stem (-एको भए) paired with -नेथिएँ, matching the first person.
The apodosis must agree in person with the subject (म requires बोक्नेथिएँ, not third-person बोक्थ्यो).
A counterfactual hypothetical if-clause cannot resolve in a present indicative verb (आउँछ).

quiz.question: If you had informed me, I would have arrived at the airport: तिमीले खबर गरेको भए म विमानस्थल ___।
quiz.explanation: Past unreal counterfactuals with first-person 'I' conclude with -नेथिएँ (आउनेथिएँ).

quiz.question: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home: भोलि पानी परे हामी घरमै ___।
quiz.explanation: A realistic future conditional using -ए resolves naturally with the future indicative बस्नेछौँ.

quiz.question: Had he taken the medicine properly, he would not have fallen sick: औषधि खाएको भए ऊ बिरामी ___।
quiz.explanation: Third-person singular negative counterfactual past uses हुने थिएन.

quiz.question: Which suffix attaches to the verb root to construct the conditional clause 'if (one does)':
quiz.explanation: The suffix -ए (e.g. गरे, गए, खाए) functions as the core synthetic conditional marker in Nepali.

tip: Think of -एको भए as 'had [verb] happened' and -नेथियो as 'would have happened'—this direct pair is the key to mastering Nepali counterfactuals.
